about: The block product's declared actions, run by the generic executor (package declared). Each action names where it runs, its parameters, what its invocation records, one or more variants (the first whose condition holds runs), each with its command as a template, a timeout, a decoding of the answer and the citation of the product's command and flags, read at read_at. Every substituted value is one shell-quoted word. Outcomes of error bodies come from outcomes.json, by (decode.action or the verb, decode.path, code). Templates name config.<key> (the shared configuration below), a parameter, <subject param>.<field> (name, nqn, layout_id, status_addr: the current host's status address, holder_alive: the recorded holder runs), variant, and in a decoding answer.<field>, stderr or exit. Every action has a runner deadline: the RUNNER's bound on one operation, never a product bound and never a checker's. A declared command runs detached on its node (its output and exit code in files under runner_io_dir, polled), so nothing can hold the runner past the deadline; at it the command's session is killed, the operation completes unknown with the detail 'timeout after <n>s', and any process that survives the kill is recorded under 'abandoned' by pid and start time. A declared deadline lies above the command's own bound, so it ends only a call that does not answer. An exception's deadline grows by its plus_param's seconds (a wait the step may set). The exceptions are the actions that stay Go handlers, each with its reason.

read.stderr_why: a failed show answers exit 1 with nothing on stdout; only stderr says why (the master refused a reserved volume, or did not answer), which the checkers need to tell apart. Comparisons ignore it (checkers/product_block.py)

steps.name: dirs
command:
import json,sys,urllib.request,urllib.parse,urllib.error
d,pre=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]; out=[]; last=""
while True:
    q=urllib.parse.urlencode({"limit":1000,"lastFileName":last,"namePattern":pre+"*"})
    try:
        r=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(d+"/?"+q,headers={"Accept":"application/json"}),timeout=10))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        if e.code==404 and not last: break
        raise
    es=r.get("Entries") or []
    out+=[e["FullPath"].rsplit("/",1)[1] for e in es]
    if not r.get("ShouldDisplayLoadMore") or not es: break
    last=es[-1]["FullPath"].rsplit("/",1)[1]
print(json.dumps(sorted(n for n in out if n.startswith(pre))))

runner_setup.why: writes the cluster spec file the blockmaster reads and the runner's own record of each volume (hosts, ports, NQN); it calls no product command or API and records nothing in the history
computes one run's ports, work directory and NQN prefix from port_base and the run's tag and sets them as vars; no command runs and nothing is recorded
closes the run's history file (its end record) so a later phase judges a whole history; a runner bookkeeping step with no product call

exceptions.why: starts a long-lived holder process and credits readiness only to it: free endpoints before the launch, the child's pid and start time recorded as owned, a readiness wait polling its status and its listeners, then the kernel NVMe/TCP connect and the device lookup
exceptions.declarable_with: a long-lived process step: launch detached, record its identity as owned, and a readiness probe polled until a declared condition holds (status JSON serving above the recorded epoch, listeners held by that pid), then dependent steps (connect, device lookup) run only after it

exceptions.why: writes through the kernel block device: the device is looked up by the volume's NQN, the block is generated and its hash checked before the invocation, one invocation per lba; the I/O runs detached under the guest device_io_runner_deadline_seconds, so a child stuck on a dead device is abandoned and recorded, never waited on
exceptions.declarable_with: a device step: resolve the guest device from the subject (NQN to /dev path) as a declared lookup, plus a runner-side generated input whose hash is recorded before the invocation; then one invocation per element of a list param

exceptions.why: reads through the kernel block device: device lookup by NQN, then dd per lba, one invocation each; the I/O runs detached under the guest device_io_runner_deadline_seconds, so a child stuck on a dead device is abandoned and recorded, never waited on
exceptions.declarable_with: a device step (the declared NQN-to-device lookup) and one invocation per element of a list param, with a result field read from stdout by a pattern (the sha256)

exceptions.why: fsync of the kernel block device, found by its NQN; the I/O runs detached under the guest device_io_runner_deadline_seconds, so a child stuck on a dead device is abandoned and recorded, never waited on
exceptions.declarable_with: a device step (the declared NQN-to-device lookup); with it the fsync is one declared command

exceptions.why: the planned hand-over is steps that feed each other: the guest disconnect, detach --plain whose sealed generation the revoke takes, a wait for the holder's own exit by its recorded identity, and a poll for the master's recorded ACK. Any failed step makes the operation unknown, not the step's own outcome, because the earlier steps already changed state (outcomes.json, the stop's revoke rows); so it is not a sequence whose outcome is its worst step's
exceptions.declarable_with: a step sequence with data passed between steps (the sealed generation parsed from detach feeds revoke), waits for a process's exit by its recorded identity and a poll for an answer line, and an outcome rule other than the worst step's (any failure after the first change is unknown)

exceptions.why: the stop's hand-over (see v3_op_stop), then move --clean, whose answer must name this move (volume, request, epoch, target) before the runner's record of the current host changes
exceptions.declarable_with: the stop's step sequence (see v3_op_stop), then a command whose answer must match the operation's own args before a subject field (the current host) is updated

exceptions.why: a fault: the process is resolved from the run's ownership ledger and killed by its recorded identity, and the kill is certified by its exit
exceptions.declarable_with: process identity from the run's ownership ledger as a subject, a kill command bound to that identity, and a wait for the exit certified by a successful check

exceptions.why: a fault's repair: restarts the killed process with the command line it ran, recorded in the ledger, and waits for readiness as attach does
exceptions.declarable_with: the ledger subject (see v3_op_kill) plus the long-lived process step of v3_op_attach, relaunching the recorded command line

exceptions.why: an observation of health after faults: polls the master and every live holder within a bound
exceptions.declarable_with: an observation over every subject of a kind (the master and each live holder) polled until a declared health condition holds within a bound

guest.about: Runner settings for the guest, the kernel NVMe/TCP host the runner connects to a volume. They are not product facts and never checker bounds. A run names its connect with the run var connect.select_var; absent, it is the default.
guest.device_io_runner_deadline_about: The RUNNER's own bound on one read, write or flush through the kernel block device, not a product bound. Under the product's plain connect the kernel keeps I/O to a dead controller blocked for ctrl_loss_tmo (600 s by default), so the runner runs the I/O detached, ends the operation as unknown at this deadline and records the abandoned child by pid and start time. It lies above fast_io_fail_tmo of every connect variant.

connect.about: A variant is DECLARED here, named, with its source and evidence false; a run selects one by name with the run var select_var (a scenario env value), and empty selects the default. Its options go into the kernel's fabrics connect string under the kernel's option names, in the order of options (the runner connects through /dev/nvme-fabrics, not nvme-cli, whose flags are --ctrl-loss-tmo, --reconnect-delay, --fast_io_fail_tmo, --keep-alive-tmo). A variant's option names may be written with _ or -; an unknown name, a value that is not an integer, or a name given twice refuses the description at load. A variant is named 'guest connect variant: <values>' in the run header and in every attach, is never release evidence, and no checker changes with it.

variants.name: fast_faults
variants.why: more fault cycles per hour: I/O to a dead controller fails after 5 s and the controller is dropped after 60 s. Its results never stand in for the plain connect's, and no checker changes between the two; the run header and every attach name it as 'guest connect variant: <values>'.
